seismology.goal: An earthquake sends compressional waves through rock at speed v _ p and slower shear waves at v _ s. A seismometer records the second kind arriving a time T after the first. Write how far away, L, the quake happened.
seismology.name: Hypocentre from two arrivals
seismology.form: T * v _ p * v _ s / ( v _ p - v _ s )
seismology.ask: Find L in kilometres for a 2 second gap, with P = 6.0 km/s and S = 3.5 km/s.
seismology.method: The slow wave takes d/v_s, the fast one d/v_p; their difference is Δt. Solve for d.

radiochemistry.goal: Every nucleus in a collection of N has the same small chance of decaying each second, set by the half-life T. Write how many decays happen per second, A.
radiochemistry.name: Activity of a radioactive source
radiochemistry.ask: Find A in becquerels for one gram of radium-226: N = 2.66e21 nuclei and T = 5.05e10 seconds.
radiochemistry.method: The decay constant is λ = ln 2 / T, and each second λN of the N nuclei decay.

decay_chains.goal: A long-lived parent (half-life T _ 1) feeds a short-lived daughter (half-life T _ 2). After a while the daughter is made as fast as it decays and its amount stops changing. Write how many daughter nuclei M sit alongside N parent nuclei.
decay_chains.name: Secular equilibrium
decay_chains.ask: Find M for a speck of radium holding N = 1e12 nuclei (T = 5.05e10 s), with its radon (R = 3.30e5 s).
decay_chains.method: When nothing changes, the daughter decays as fast as it forms: λ₂M = λ₁N, and each λ is ln 2 over its half-life.

distributions.goal: Add up many small independent random pushes and the total spreads into a bell-shaped curve with centre μ and width σ. Write the height f of that curve at the value x.
distributions.name: Gaussian density
distributions.ask: Find f at one width from the centre: x = 1, μ = 0, σ = 1.
distributions.method: The central limit theorem: sums of many independent pieces tend to this curve; the factor in front makes its total area 1.

bayesian_inference.goal: A condition affects a fraction p of people. A check comes back positive with probability L when it is present, and wrongly with probability F when it is not. Write the chance Q that someone who checks positive really has it.
bayesian_inference.name: Bayes' rule
bayesian_inference.ask: Find Q for a condition in 1% of people, a check that finds it 99% of the time and gives false alarms 5% of the time.

vars.L: chance of a positive when present

bayesian_inference.method: Of all the positives, the true ones are L·p and the false ones F·(1 − p). Q is the true share.

equivalence_principle.goal: A hammer and a feather are dropped together from height h in a vacuum. They land at the same moment, because a body's inertia and its weight are always in proportion. Write how long t they take to reach the ground under acceleration g.
equivalence_principle.name: Universality of free fall
equivalence_principle.ask: Find t in seconds for the drop made on the Moon in 1971: h = 1.6 m, g = 1.62 m/s².
equivalence_principle.method: Starting from rest with constant acceleration, h = ½gt². The mass of the body appears nowhere.

gravitational_time_dilation.goal: A clock sits a distance r from the centre of a mass M. Compared with a clock far away it ticks slower. Write how many seconds τ it counts while the faraway clock counts t.
gravitational_time_dilation.name: Gravitational time dilation
gravitational_time_dilation.ask: Find τ in seconds for one hour on the surface of a neutron star: M = 2.8e30 kg, r = 12 km (G and c in SI units).
gravitational_time_dilation.method: The Schwarzschild metric: for a clock at rest at radius r, dτ² = (1 − 2GM/rc²) dt².
